# Super Day Behavioral Round

[← JPMorgan](../README.md) · [Every JPMorgan question](../../jpmorgan.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/superday-behavioral-round)

`leadership` `project-deep-dive`

---

## Requirements

- Have STAR stories ready for common prompts:
  - Take me through a previous project and clarify what you personally did.
  - Discuss a project you are proud of or an assignment you found difficult.
  - Describe a roadblock you encountered and the way you addressed it.
  - Share an example of a disagreement with a teammate or coworker.
  - Talk about a time when you demonstrated leadership.
  - Explain how you supported a coworker or strengthened collaboration within the team.
- Be prepared for a hiring manager to ask follow-up questions about your resume and projects.
- Keep your responses brief enough to reserve time for the candidate's questions.

## Notes

- Behavioral interviewers may be relaxed and conversational, while others may enter notes as you speak; regard either style as an assessed round.
- One candidate interpreted a question as testing their readiness to work overtime. A measured response should highlight accountability, escalation, prioritization, and sustainable execution instead of merely committing to unlimited hours.
- The behavioral discussion is often paired with straightforward coding and high-level system design, which can make strong stories a distinguishing factor.

## Preparation

- Develop six STAR stories and connect each to several themes, including conflict, ambiguity, ownership, leadership, failure, and helping others.
- Include a technical point, a business result, and a collaboration point in every project story.
- Rehearse both a two-minute and a five-minute telling of each story.
